queue.source: relation_audit/dispositions.json entries with disposition == "certificate-required" and 1 <= section <= 5

outcomeVocabulary.description: A kind-correct typed Certificate exists in the section module.
No seven-kind certificate is honest; a target category and rationale are recorded.

targetCategoryVocabularyNote: No row in this fragment is reclassified: every sections 1-5 certificate-required row fits a seven-kind certificate without weakening the statement.
nonClaims: This fragment is not a production registry and does not claim 136/136 or resolved coverage.
A certified definitionalIdentity is a fresh `DefEq`/`rfl` check, not propositional equality and not a physical-identity claim.

The §2 value-level bridge rows are certified as observationalEquivalence over an explicit channel; this is not a claim that the two quantities are propositionally equivalent (`↔`), and it is not a definitional identity.
The kernel pins have empty pairIds and do not claim a cross-theory pair edge.
No conditionalComposition certificate is created in this fragment; no parent chain is invented.
Reusing the original theorem does not make the source statement an audit verdict; the certificate records only the declared typed relation.

channels.name: transferCoefficient
channels.leftObs: fun δ x => BEP.transfer δ.lam x
channels.rightObs: fun δ x => Hammond.tsCoord δ.lam x

statementProvenance.note: The delivered theorem is a non-definitional equality of two real-valued observables (`field_simp`, not `rfl`), so it cannot be a definitionalIdentity; it is also not a propositional `↔`, so it is not labelled `equivalence`. It is certified as an observationalEquivalence over the declared transferCoefficient channel: at every driving force and every context with lam != 0 the two theory observables agree, which is exactly the delivered statement.

entries.kindJustification: The source theorem proves `BEP.transfer lam x = Hammond.tsCoord lam x` for every `x` when `lam != 0` (by `field_simp`, not `rfl`). The certificate's `transferCoefficient` channel observes BEP.transfer on the left and Hammond.tsCoord on the right over all real driving forces; its `sound` field is exactly the delivered theorem. This is an observational claim about two theory observables, not a propositional equivalence of two predicates and not a definitional identity.

r2Ledger.rationale: Genuine equivalence between the BEP observable secant slope and the Hammond Leffler secant. The bodies differ in sign convention and pair indexing, so this is a theorem-level equivalence, not an rfl identity; it is a direct Hammond-BEP relation.
r2Ledger.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate; do not close it by rfl.

channels.name: windowSecantSlope
channels.leftObs: fun δ p => BEP.secSlope δ.lam p.1 p.2
channels.rightObs: fun δ p => Hammond.lefflerSecant δ.lam p.1 (p.1 + p.2)

statementProvenance.note: The delivered theorem is a non-definitional equality of two real-valued observables (`ring` after unfolding, not `rfl`; the bodies differ in sign convention and pair indexing), so it is not a definitionalIdentity and not a propositional `↔`. It is certified as an observationalEquivalence over the declared windowSecantSlope channel: for every window `(x,h)` the two observables agree, which is exactly the delivered statement. No non-degeneracy premise is needed because both divisions are totalised and the theorem holds at h = 0.

entries.kindJustification: The source theorem proves `BEP.secSlope lam x h = Hammond.lefflerSecant lam x (x+h)` for every window `(x,h)` (by `ring`, not `rfl`; the bodies differ in sign convention and pair indexing). The certificate's `windowSecantSlope` channel observes the two window slopes over all `(x,h)`; its `sound` field is exactly the delivered theorem. This is an observational claim about two theory observables, not a propositional equivalence and not a definitional identity.
